name: Bellanca 14-13 Cruisair
summary: Postwar four-seat, wood-and-fabric low-wing tourer with fixed conventional gear, recognized by the oval end-plate fins on its horizontal tail ('cardboard Constellation').

engines: Single flat-six Franklin (150–165 hp) in a smooth cowl
fuselage: Fabric-covered steel-tube fuselage with a four-seat cabin
Fixed main gear with a tailwheel
tail: Central fin plus an oval end-plate fin on each horizontal stabilizer (triple-fin look)

tellTales: Triple-fin tail on a low-wing four-seater
Fixed main gear with a tailwheel on a low-wing airplane
Oval end-plate fins on the horizontal tail

confusedWith.howToTell: The Cruisair has fixed gear and a smaller engine; the Cruisemaster is a more powerful retractable version with the same triple tail.
The Cruisair is a low-wing four-seater with a triple fin; the Luscombe is a high-wing two-seater.
The Cruisair has a triple-fin tail and a tailwheel; the PA-28 has a single fin and a nosewheel.
The Cruisair has a triple-fin tail and a tailwheel; the Navion has a single fin, a nosewheel and a long canopy.
